case_name: Simple direct ownership — single blocked owner above 50%

computation.description: Identify blocked owners
Sum all ownership by blocked persons in X
Aggregate blocked ownership of X
Apply 50% rule

blocked_verdicts.verdict: blocked — aggregate ownership by blocked persons = 60% ≥ 50%

guidance_basis: OFAC FAQ 398: entities owned 50% or more in the aggregate by blocked persons are blocked; direct ownership test
weakest_point: The 60% threshold is chosen as a clean above-threshold case; exact published example numbers may differ.

case_name: Two blocked owners — convergent paths from distinct blocked persons

computation.description: Identify blocked owners
computation.calculation: A is blocked; B is blocked

computation.description: Sum all ownership by blocked persons in X (aggregate, not per-person threshold)
Aggregate blocked ownership of X
Apply 50% rule: aggregate vs. aggregate, not per-person
computation.result: 70% ≥ 50% → X is blocked. Each individual owner's share (30% or 40%) does NOT meet the 50% test alone; the aggregate does.

guidance_basis: OFAC FAQ 398/401: the 50% rule is an aggregate test; the contributions of multiple blocked persons are summed; neither A nor B individually exceeds 50%, yet X is still blocked
weakest_point: The key nuance — that neither A nor B individually reaches 50% yet X is still blocked — is the most commonly misunderstood aspect of this case.

case_name: Chain through majority-owned intermediary — indirect ownership via full attribution

computation.description: Identify blocked owners and test direct ownership of X
computation.calculation: A is blocked; A does not own X directly

computation.description: Test: does any blocked person own ≥50% of Y?
Full attribution through ≥50%-owned intermediary: A is blocked, A owns ≥50% of Y → Y is a blocked entity
Attribute Y's ownership of X to A (full attribution, NOT multiplicative)
computation.calculation: Y→X = 50% attributed to A as A's indirect ownership of X

computation.description: A's aggregate ownership of X
Apply 50% rule through intermediary chain
Verify: multiplicative alternative (60% × 50% = 30%) would give 30% < 50%, which is WRONG under OFAC guidance
computation.result: OFAC uses full attribution, not multiplicative calculation — this is the critical distinction

blocked_verdicts.verdict: blocked — owned ≥50% by blocked person A
blocked — A's aggregate ownership = 50% via full attribution through Y; A also indirectly holds 50% of X through Y (Y itself is 60% owned by A)

guidance_basis: OFAC FAQ 399/401: if a blocked person owns 50% or more of an entity, that entity's entire holdings in other entities are attributed to the blocked person (full attribution). NOT multiplicative. A owning 60% of Y → Y is blocked → Y's 50% of X is attributed 100% to A.
weakest_point: The distinction between full attribution (correct) and multiplicative (wrong) is the load-bearing rule here. My certainty that OFAC uses full attribution is high based on FAQ 399/401, but the exact wording distinguishing this from a purely multiplicative approach should be verified against the most current FAQ version.

case_name: Convergent paths — same blocked owner through two intermediaries; contributions summed

computation.description: Test: does A own ≥50% of Y1?
Test: does A own ≥50% of Y2?
Attribute Y1's ownership of X to A (full attribution)
computation.calculation: Y1→X = 30% → A gets 30% indirect of X

computation.description: Attribute Y2's ownership of X to A (full attribution)
computation.calculation: Y2→X = 25% → A gets 25% indirect of X

computation.description: A's aggregate ownership of X — convergent paths are SUMMED
computation.calculation: A direct of X = 0% + 30% (via Y1) + 25% (via Y2) = 55%

computation.description: Apply 50% rule to aggregate
Edge order independence check
computation.calculation: Y1→X contribution + Y2→X contribution = 55% regardless of evaluation order
computation.result: Graph is commutative — serialization does not affect result

blocked_verdicts.verdict: blocked — A's aggregate ownership = 55% (30%+25%) ≥ 50% via convergent paths through two majority-owned intermediaries

guidance_basis: OFAC FAQ 398/401: convergent paths through separate majority-owned intermediaries are summed to compute the blocked owner's aggregate ownership of the target. Both Y1 and Y2 are blocked (≥50% owned by A), so both of their stakes in X are attributed to A and summed.
weakest_point: In this graph, Y1 and Y2 do not directly overlap in ownership of X (30%+25%=55%), which is unambiguous. In a more complex graph where two blocked intermediaries each own ≥50% of a third entity, the aggregation is still additive (not multiplicative) per OFAC guidance.

case_name: Mixed ownership — blocked and non-blocked owners; convergent paths with a non-controlling stake

computation.description: Identify blocked owners
computation.calculation: A blocked; B blocked; C NOT blocked

computation.description: Include only blocked persons in the aggregate
Aggregate blocked ownership of X
Apply 50% rule to blocked aggregate only
Common error: including non-blocked ownership in denominator or treating it as diluting the blocked aggregate
computation.calculation: Wrong method: blocked 65 + non-blocked 35 = 100 total; blocked/total = 65% — same numerically here but conceptually wrong; the rule is not 50% of total shares, it is 50% of aggregate blocked ownership regardless of who holds the rest

blocked_verdicts.verdict: blocked — aggregate blocked ownership = 65% ≥ 50%; C's 35% stake does not insulate X

guidance_basis: OFAC FAQ 398: the 50% rule does not require that blocked persons own a majority of the entity outright; if the aggregate of all blocked ownership meets 50%, the entity is blocked. Non-blocked ownership (C's 35%) does not offset or reduce blocked aggregate for purposes of the test.
weakest_point: The non-blocked person's stake (35%) is included in the total ownership of X, but does not affect whether X is blocked under the 50% rule. If X had other non-blocked owners whose stakes were large enough to make the blocked aggregate fall below 50%, X would escape the block. Some implementations erroneously include non-blocked ownership as a 'dilution' factor — it does not.
